samples.summary: Enabling offline persistence while an editor is open unmounts the DocumentProvider, discarding the unsent change queue
samples.evidence: `if (!ready) return null;` (line 273) runs on every render, with `ready = settled && identified`. `settled` comes from `useDurableDocument`, where `settled: !eligible || answered` and `answered = decision?.subject === subject` with `subject = `${eligible}\0${userId}\0${docKey}`` (use-durable-document.ts:179, 225, 247). When the preference flips from off to on for an already-open document, `eligibleNow` rises (the latch at use-durable-document.ts:161-163 deliberately allows rising), `subject` changes, `answered` becomes false and `settled` becomes false — so `ready` is false and `CollabDocumentProvider` returns `null`, unmounting `DocumentProvider` and the whole editor subtree in that commit, before the election effect can resolve. The file's own comment (lines 204-218) states that unmounting the `DocumentProvider` "discard[s] the Yorkie change queue, which on a document with unsent edits is the loss this whole feature exists to prevent". This is reachable from the advertised flow: the sync chip only offers `Turn on for later documents` while `state === 'not-saved'`, i.e. precisely when unsent edits exist (sync-status-chip.tsx:146, 240) — so clicking the offer destroys the work it was warning about. It also fires for every open editor when the toggle is flipped in Settings or in another tab. The existing durable suite only covers the preference being turned *off* mid-open ('keeps its client when the preference changes underneath it'), never turned on.

samples.summary: Election acquired but never used after the preference is enabled mid-open, blocking a second tab from durability
samples.evidence: `if (ready && held.current?.subject !== subject) { held.current = { subject, durable, clientKey }; }` — `subject` here is `${me?.id}:${docKey}` and does *not* include eligibility, so once latched with `durable: false` (preference off at open time) it is never re-latched. Meanwhile `useDurableDocument` does re-decide when eligibility rises and acquires the `wb-durable:{userId}:{docKey}` Web Lock (use-durable-document.ts:185-214). The consumer ignores the result and stays non-durable, but the lock is held for the life of the open document and is never `standDown()`n. Another tab opening the same document is then refused durability by `acquireDurableSession` while no tab is actually persisting it — the exact state `standDown` exists to avoid.

samples.summary: logout() erases local data (including the only copy of unreconciled work) before it knows the sign-out succeeded
samples.evidence: `await eraseOfflineDataOnLogout({ keepArchives: eraseLocalData === 'keep-archives' })` is placed at line 125, *before* `if (res && !res.ok && !suppressFailure) throw new Error('Failed to log out')` at line 129. On a 5xx from `/auth/logout` the user is still signed in and sees a failure, but their archives — which this feature documents as "the only copy of work the server never took" (offline-erase.ts:188-192) — have already been destroyed with `keepArchives: false`. The behaviour is also inconsistent with the network-failure path, where the `catch` at line 106 rethrows before the erase and the data survives.

samples.summary: The durable provider's WafflebaseDocStore is never closed, leaking an IndexedDB connection per document opened
samples.evidence: `const store = useMemo(() => new WafflebaseDocStore({...}), [userId])` has no matching cleanup effect calling `store.close()` on unmount. A grep for `.close()` across packages/frontend/src shows closes only in `offline-runtime.tsx:160` and `offline-erase.ts` (230/262/296/367) — nothing in `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx`. Each durable document opened in a session therefore leaves an open `IDBDatabase` connection alive for the life of the tab; a connection left open can also block another tab's `versionchange`/`deleteDatabase` until the `onversionchange` handler fires. The same leak exists for the fallback store created in `offline-erase.ts:413` (`store() ?? new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId: who })`), which is likewise never closed.

samples.summary: deleteDocuments turns a successful deletion into a rejection when the body parses to null
samples.evidence: `const result = (await response.json()) as { deleted: string[] };` followed by `result.deleted ?? []` — if the endpoint answers with a literal `null` body (valid JSON), `result` is `null` and `result.deleted` throws a TypeError, so `deleteDocuments` rejects after the server has already deleted the documents. The previous code (`return response.json()`) propagated `null` harmlessly. `result?.deleted ?? []` would preserve the old behaviour.

samples.summary: `stoodDown` is never cleared, so a subject that recurs stays permanently non-durable
samples.evidence: `const [stoodDown, setStoodDown] = useState<string | null>(null)` is only ever set (never reset), and `decided` is gated on `stoodDown !== subject`. If the same `${userId}:${docKey}` subject is reached again in the same component instance — e.g. the identity flips 7 → 9 → 7 while the route stays mounted, which the file's own comment says React Query focus-refetch can cause — the stale stand-down still applies and the document is refused durability for no current reason.

samples.summary: Adding `offerOffline` to the toast effect's deps restarts the debounce and re-raises the warning after the offer is accepted
samples.evidence: The effect deps became `[stranded, state, connected, offerOffline, turnOnOfflineSaving]`. Clicking the offer flips `offerOffline` true → false while `stranded` is still true, so the cleanup clears the pending timer and a fresh `TOAST_DELAY_MS` timer is scheduled, re-firing `toast.warning('Not saved', { id: TOAST_ID, ... })` two seconds after the user has just acknowledged it.

verdict.reason: The mechanism reproduces exactly as described in the repository. `collab-document-provider.tsx:273-275` returns `null` unconditionally whenever `ready` (=`settled && identified`, line 241) is false — it is not qualified by the already-`held` decision. `settled` can fall from true to false mid-open: the eligibility latch at `use-durable-document.ts:157-163` is keyed on `userId + docKey` only and deliberately allows eligibility to RISE, `subject` at :179 embeds `eligible`, so a preference flip off->on changes `subject`, makes `answered` false (:225) and `settled: !eligible || answered` false (:247). The re-decision effect (:185-214) only runs after commit and resolves asynchronously, so at least one commit renders null — unmounting `DocumentProvider` and the editor subtree, which the file's own comment at collab-document-provider.tsx:204-218 says discards the Yorkie change queue, "the loss this whole feature exists to prevent". The flip is live-observable mid-open via `useSyncExternalStore` + CHANGE_EVENT/storage subscription (offline-persistence-preference.ts:102-121, 61-73), and is triggered from inside a mounted editor by the chip's offer, which appears precisely when unsent edits exist (sync-status-chip.tsx:146, 238-242, 292) — whose own comment at :148-153 asserts the tear-down is avoided. Existing coverage only tests the off direction (collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:310-330). I considered refuting as already-guarded because the pin `@yorkie-js/react: 0.7.22` (package.json:66) is below `MinClientKeyVersion 0.7.23` (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24), making `supportsClientKey()` false and the path inert today; I declined because vite.config.ts:408-418 documents that bumping the dependency is the only action needed to enable it, and the suite mocks the capability true as the intended configuration — a rollout version flag does not make the logic defect unreal, and its cost when it fires is loss of unsent edits (critical).

finding.summary: Election acquired but never used after the preference is enabled mid-open, blocking a second tab from durability
finding.evidence: `if (ready && held.current?.subject !== subject) { held.current = { subject, durable, clientKey }; }` — `subject` here is `${me?.id}:${docKey}` and does *not* include eligibility, so once latched with `durable: false` (preference off at open time) it is never re-latched. Meanwhile `useDurableDocument` does re-decide when eligibility rises and acquires the `wb-durable:{userId}:{docKey}` Web Lock (use-durable-document.ts:185-214). The consumer ignores the result and stays non-durable, but the lock is held for the life of the open document and is never `standDown()`n. Another tab opening the same document is then refused durability by `acquireDurableSession` while no tab is actually persisting it — the exact state `standDown` exists to avoid.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `collab-document-provider.tsx:229` builds `subject` as `${me?.id ?? 'anon'}:${docKey}` with no eligibility term, and `:242-244` only re-latches when that subject changes — so a document opened with the preference off stays latched `{durable:false, clientKey:undefined}` forever. Meanwhile `use-durable-document.ts:159-163` deliberately lets eligibility RISE mid-open, `:179` folds it into its own subject, and `:185-214` then calls `acquireDurableSession(userId, docKey)`, taking the `wb-durable:{userId}:{docKey}` Web Lock (`durable-session.ts:69-71, 139-168`) and holding it until unmount. The consumer ignores the result and renders the non-durable `inner`. Nothing releases it: `standDown` is only invoked from `onLockRefused` on `DurableYorkieProvider` (`collab-document-provider.tsx:296`), which is mounted only on the `decided.durable` branch that is not taken here; grep shows no other non-test caller. A second tab requesting the same name is then refused (`durable-session.ts:93-97`, `160-168`) while no tab persists the document. The trigger is a first-class in-app flow, not hypothetical: the preference is a live `useSyncExternalStore` across tabs and same-tab events (`offline-persistence-preference.ts:102-121`), and `SyncStatusChip`, mounted inside the open editor, offers exactly this mid-open enable (`sync-status-chip.tsx:146-158`). Corroborating: the rise also flips `settled` false (`use-durable-document.ts:247`), making `collab-document-provider.tsx:273-275` return `null` and unmount the editor subtree — the teardown the chip's comment promises will not occur. No guard, no unreachability, squarely in the correctness lane (leaked resource + broken multi-tab invariant on a reachable path).

finding.summary: logout() erases local data (including the only copy of unreconciled work) before it knows the sign-out succeeded
finding.evidence: `await eraseOfflineDataOnLogout({ keepArchives: eraseLocalData === 'keep-archives' })` is placed at line 125, *before* `if (res && !res.ok && !suppressFailure) throw new Error('Failed to log out')` at line 129. On a 5xx from `/auth/logout` the user is still signed in and sees a failure, but their archives — which this feature documents as "the only copy of work the server never took" (offline-erase.ts:188-192) — have already been destroyed with `keepArchives: false`. The behaviour is also inconsistent with the network-failure path, where the `catch` at line 106 rethrows before the erase and the data survives.

verdict.reason: The claimed ordering is real and verbatim: auth.ts:125-127 performs the irreversible erase before the failure check at auth.ts:129-131. With default options (eraseLocalData "all", suppressFailure false — used by nav-user.tsx:41), a non-ok /auth/logout response (proxy 502/503, restart, gateway error) destroys archives via eraseOfflineDataOnLogout -> dropAllForUser (offline-erase.ts:200-223) and clears the recorded identity, then throws "Failed to log out" while the session cookie was never cleared (backend auth.controller.ts:98-101 clears cookies only when the handler runs). Those archives are documented at offline-erase.ts:188-192 as the only copy of work the server never took, so the loss is unrecoverable. The asymmetry with the network-error path is also confirmed: the catch at auth.ts:106-110 rethrows before the erase, so a thrown fetch spares the data while a 5xx does not. Existing tests (tests/api/auth.test.ts:102-151) cover only 200 and 401, so no guard or caller makes this unreachable. Data loss on a path reachable in normal use is in the correctness lane and blocking.

finding.summary: An involuntary 401 erases the local live entries, which include the un-pushed change log — destroying the only durable copy of unsent work
finding.evidence: `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm calls `logout({... eraseLocalData: "keep-archives"})`, which reaches `dropAllForUser(userId, {keepArchives:true})` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1031). That loop calls `this.purge(docKey)` for every header, and `purge` deletes the CHANGES range as well as the snapshot. The justification in the comment — "The live entries still go. They are copies of content the server holds, so nothing is lost by dropping them" — is false for the log: the store's own eviction logic says the opposite (`evictOldest` skips any entry with `changeCount > 0` because "this store cannot tell an acked change from an unacked one", wafflebase-doc-store.ts). So a session that expires (or any transient 401 from a restarted backend) while a durable document holds un-pushed edits deletes exactly the work the feature exists to preserve; the redirect to /login is refusable (see the `redirectTo` comment about `beforeunload`, auth.ts:47-60), so the tab can keep running and then lose the edits on the next reload.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. fetchWithAuth's 401 arm (auth.ts:250-269) calls logout with eraseLocalData:"keep-archives", which flows through eraseOfflineDataOnLogout (auth.ts:125-127; offline-erase.ts:200-231) to dropAllForUser(userId,{keepArchives:true}) (offline-erase.ts:31). dropAllForUser purges every header key for the user unconditionally (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1036-1058) with no changeCount or isLive exemption, and purge deletes the CHANGES range along with snapshot and header (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:827-835). keepArchives only skips dropArchivesWhere (1071-1073), i.e. it spares the ARCHIVES store alone. The justifying comment ("copies of content the server holds, so nothing is lost") is contradicted by the store's own eviction rule, which refuses to evict any entry with changeCount > 0 because "This store cannot tell an acked change from an unacked one... a non-empty log counts as unsent" (1332-1341, check at 1362). Nothing archives live entries before this erase: remove() only archives when the expectLoss latch is set by the SDK's LocalChangesDropped handler (739-771, 791-803), which this path never sets, and OfflineRuntime only retries erases/sweeps/offers existing archives (offline-runtime.tsx:83-150). The redirect is documented as refusable via beforeunload (auth.ts:47-63), so the tab keeps running and the un-pushed log is gone on the next load. The design doc records this as intended (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:173-179, 251), but the stated premise is false for the change log, so this remains a real data-loss path on a reachable, involuntary event — critical under the correctness rubric. No refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: After a sign-out erase the still-mounted durable client re-persists the document to disk; the only write guard is the preference, not the sign-out
finding.evidence: The store is built with `isPersistenceEnabled: getOfflinePersistenceEnabled` and nothing else. `refuseIfDisabled` therefore only blocks writes when the *preference* is off. On the 401 path, `dropAllForUser` purges the entries and marks them evicted, so the client's next `appendChange` throws — which makes the SDK write a fresh `saveSnapshot`, and `saveSnapshot` does `this.evicted.delete(docKey)` and writes the document back (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:580-600). Because the 401 redirect is refusable (auth.ts:47-60: a `beforeunload` guard — which the sync chip registers precisely when there are unsent edits — lets the user cancel and the page keeps running), the erase promised on sign-out is undone and a signed-out account's document content is back on a possibly shared disk, with nothing scheduled to remove it again.

verdict.reason: Verified the full chain in the repo. The durable store is constructed with only `isPersistenceEnabled: getOfflinePersistenceEnabled` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:131-149), and `refuseIfDisabled` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:382-391) gates writes solely on that localStorage preference — there is no sign-out/session term. `dropAllForUser` purges and marks keys evicted (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1050-1057); a later `appendChange` therefore throws via `refuseIfEvicted` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:653-656, 711-720), which the module's own comments say provokes the SDK into writing a fresh snapshot — and `saveSnapshot` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:580-600) passes only `refuseIfDisabled`, rewrites snapshot+header, and clears the evicted marker, restoring the erased content with a fresh `updatedAt`. The sign-out paths (auth.ts:125-139 and the 401 arm at auth.ts:250-269) leave the client mounted: `redirectTo` is explicitly refusable (auth.ts:65-74) and sync-status-chip.tsx:171-182 registers the `beforeunload` guard whenever there are possibly-unsent edits. No cache clear on logout exists, so CollabDocumentProvider (collab-document-provider.tsx:277-300) keeps `me` and keeps DurableYorkieProvider mounted, and neither offline-erase.ts nor offline-runtime.tsx installs a post-sign-out write latch. Real, reachable, and a broken invariant (the erase sign-out promises is silently undone) within the correctness lane.

finding.summary: An election is acquired but never used when eligibility rises after the provider latched non-durable, holding the per-document lock and denying durability to every other tab
finding.evidence: `held.current` is written once per `subject` (`${me.id}:${docKey}`) on the first `ready` render and never revisited (collab-document-provider.tsx:242-248), while `useDurableDocument` keeps re-deciding: its `latched` eligibility is allowed to *rise* (use-durable-document.ts:159-163) and the effect then calls `acquireDurableSession` and holds `wb-durable:{user}:{docKey}` until unmount. So when the preference is switched on while a document is open — which is the chip's own primary entry point (`turnOnOfflineSaving`, sync-status-chip.tsx:148) — this tab takes and keeps the election for a document it will never persist. Any other tab that opens the same document is refused the election (`acquireDurableSession` returns undefined) and stays non-durable, so the feature the user just enabled silently does not work for that document in any tab until the holding tab closes it.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. `CollabDocumentProvider` latches its decision on `subject = ${me?.id ?? 'anon'}:${docKey}` (collab-document-provider.tsx:229, 242-244), which does not include the offline preference, so once latched non-durable the record is never revisited while the document stays open (`decided`, 245-248; durable branch gated at 277-279). Meanwhile `useDurableDocument` deliberately lets eligibility RISE (use-durable-document.ts:159-163) and includes `eligible` in its own `subject` (179), so flipping the preference changes the effect deps (214) and runs `acquireDurableSession(userId, docKey)` (198), whose handle is released only on cleanup (210-213). The lock `wb-durable:{userId}:{docKey}` (durable-session.ts:69-71) is requested with `ifAvailable: true` and returns `undefined` to any other tab (durable-session.ts:93-97, 160-167), so other tabs are refused durability. The trigger is a real, primary path: `turnOnOfflineSaving` (sync-status-chip.tsx:148-158) writes the preference with no reload, and `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled` re-renders the open provider synchronously (offline-persistence-preference.ts:61-73, 115-121). Result: the tab holds the per-document election while rendering the non-durable branch, denying durability to every other tab until the document is closed. No guard or caller elsewhere breaks this chain.
